[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

AI agents capable of autonomous task execution require a trigger mechanism that is event-driven, deterministic, and scoped to intent — yet existing CI/CD pipelines are triggered by source control events (commits, pull requests), not by work item state changes. Without a defined dispatch mechanism, autonomous agent execution remains a manual, prompt-driven process: a developer must initiate every agent interaction individually, negating the pipeline-scale productivity benefit that autonomous agents are designed to deliver.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The Label-Driven Agent Dispatch Pattern defines an event-driven pipeline architecture in which a label applied to an issue in the issue tracker acts as the execution trigger for a specialized AI agent pipeline. A label taxonomy maps intent signals (e.g., `agent:implementation`, `agent:documentation`) to specific agent configurations. The pipeline executes in three sequential stages: **Validate** (structural spec check + enterprise work item reference check), **Dispatch** (agent context assembly and invocation), and **Report** (PR creation + issue comment with results). Each stage is atomic and the pipeline fails closed at the Validate stage if the spec does not meet the quality gate.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- When building autonomous AI agent delivery pipelines that should execute without human mediation between spec completion and agent invocation
- When multiple agent types (implementation, documentation, testing, infrastructure) must share a common execution queue (the issue tracker) with routing to specialized configurations
- When agent execution must be auditable, repeatable, and subject to the same quality gates as human-authored delivery
- After PTN-APP-GOV-005 spec templates are adopted and PTN-GOV-AI-007 validation gate requirements are defined — this pattern implements both
page_texts.7:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineers** designing and operating CI/CD pipelines and agent infrastructure
- **DevOps Engineers** implementing automation workflows, event triggers, and deployment gates
- **Solutions Architects** evaluating event-driven agent orchestration for delivery pipeline integration
- **AI/ML Engineers** integrating large language model agents into structured delivery workflows
page_texts.8:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Zero-friction execution**: Label assignment is the only human action required to initiate agent execution after a spec is authored and reviewed — no manual prompt, no pipeline configuration per task
- **Intent-based routing**: The label taxonomy separates the execution trigger (`agent-task`) from the agent type (`agent:implementation`) — a single issue queue serves all agent types without pipeline proliferation
- **Fail-closed quality gate**: Structural spec validation runs before any agent invocation — malformed or incomplete specs are rejected with actionable feedback, not passed to the agent where they produce low-quality output
- **Auditable execution**: Every pipeline run is logged against the triggering issue, the spec content at trigger time, and the resulting PR — creating a full execution audit trail

page_texts.10:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [AI Agent-Driven SDLC Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md) identifies "event-driven over polling" as a core architectural principle for agent pipeline design. Polling-based agent invocation (where a pipeline periodically scans for new work) introduces latency, wastes compute, and produces no clear audit event for compliance purposes. An event-driven model — where label assignment is the state change that triggers the pipeline — is reactive, zero-latency, and produces a discrete, auditable trigger event for every execution.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Modern issue trackers support webhook-based event emission on label assignment. CI/CD platforms can subscribe to these events and execute pipeline workflows in response. This creates a complete event-driven chain:

```
Label assigned → webhook fires → CI/CD workflow triggers → pipeline executes
```

The challenge is not the event plumbing (which is standard platform capability) but the pipeline architecture: how to validate specs before agents see them, how to route to different agent configurations based on label, how to assemble the agent context window from the issue spec and enterprise context files, and how to report results back to the issue and into the PR.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

- **Manual initiation bottleneck**: Without event-driven dispatch, each agent task requires a human to manually invoke the agent — teams gain individual developer productivity but not pipeline-scale delivery throughput
- **No routing without a taxonomy**: Without a defined label taxonomy, teams create ad-hoc labels that route to overlapping or undefined agent configurations — the same work item may trigger multiple agents or none
- **Validation-free invocation**: Pipelines that pass unvalidated issue bodies directly to agents amplify spec quality problems — a malformed spec produces malformed agent output at pipeline scale
- **Silent failure**: Without a structured report-back step, agents that fail silently (no PR created, no comment posted) leave issues in an indeterminate state — the author has no signal that execution failed
page_texts.13:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- The label taxonomy must be stable — changing a label that is used as a routing key in live pipelines requires coordinated deployment of the taxonomy change and the pipeline configuration change together
- The validation gate must be fast (< 30 seconds) — slow validation creates a poor authoring feedback loop where spec authors wait too long to learn their spec is malformed
- Agent credentials must be scoped to the minimum permissions required — write access to feature branches and PR creation only; no admin or merge permissions
- The pipeline must handle agent failure gracefully — if the agent itself fails (model timeout, API error, output validation failure), the pipeline must post a failure comment on the issue with enough diagnostic information for the author to act

page_texts.15:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The Label-Driven Agent Dispatch Pattern defines a three-stage pipeline architecture:

**Stage 1 — Validate**: Structural spec validation and enterprise work item reference validation (per PTN-GOV-AI-007). Fails closed with a corrective comment if any required element is absent.

**Stage 2 — Dispatch**: Agent context assembly (spec body + injected enterprise context per PTN-APP-GOV-002) and agent invocation. The agent type is selected based on the secondary label applied to the issue.

**Stage 3 — Report**: Agent output processing, pull request creation on a feature branch, and result comment posted to the originating issue. Traceability metadata is injected into the PR body (per PTN-GOV-AI-007).

│  Labels: agent-task  ◄── Execution trigger label   │
│          agent:implementation  ◄── Routing label    │
│  Body: (PTN-APP-GOV-005 spec)                       │
└────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘

                     ▼

│                                                     │
│  1b. Cross-Reference Validation (PTN-GOV-AI-007)   │
│      ✓ WI#<id> format matches configured regex?     │
│                                                     │
│  FAIL → post corrective comment → halt             │

└────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘

                     ▼
STAGE 2: DISPATCH
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│      agent:implementation → implementation agent   │
│      agent:documentation  → documentation agent    │
│      agent:testing        → test generation agent  │
│      agent:infrastructure → IaC agent              │
│                                                     │
│  2b. Context Assembly                               │

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#label-taxonomy]

### Label Taxonomy

| Label | Role | Applied By | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-task` | **Execution trigger** | Engineer (after spec review) | Fires the dispatch pipeline |
| `agent:implementation` | Routing — code | Engineer or product owner | Routes to implementation agent configuration |
| `agent:documentation` | Routing — docs | Engineer or product owner | Routes to documentation agent configuration |
| `agent:testing` | Routing — tests | Engineer or product owner | Routes to test generation agent configuration |
| `agent:infrastructure` | Routing — IaC | Engineer or product owner | Routes to infrastructure provisioning agent |
| `agent:blocked` | Status | Pipeline (on failure) | Indicates pipeline failure; agent did not execute |
| `agent:complete` | Status | Pipeline (on success) | Indicates PR was opened; awaiting review |

> **Governance rule**: The `agent-task` label must only be applied after the spec has been authored and peer-reviewed. Applying the label is the approval signal that the spec is ready for agent execution — it is the equivalent of moving a card to "In Development."
page_texts.18:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#branch-and-pr-naming-convention]

### Branch and PR Naming Convention

| Element | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Feature branch | `agent/<issue-number>-<goal-slug>` | `agent/88-add-rate-limiting` |
| PR title | `[AGENT] <goal> (#<issue>)` | `[AGENT] Add rate limiting to API gateway (#88)` |
| PR body (required block) | See below | — |

**Required PR body traceability block** (injected by pipeline, not by agent):

```markdown
## Traceability

- **Enterprise Work Item**: WI#4821
- **Agent Task Issue**: #88
- **Agent Type**: implementation
- **Model**: (injected at runtime)
- **Generated**: (ISO 8601 timestamp)
```

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#step-1--define-the-label-taxonomy-in-the-issue-tracker]

### Step 1 — Define the Label Taxonomy in the Issue Tracker

Create all labels in the issue tracker before deploying any pipeline. Assign consistent colors to aid visual scanning:

- Green family: routing labels (`agent:implementation`, `agent:documentation`, etc.)
- Blue: execution trigger (`agent-task`)
- Yellow: status in-progress (`agent:complete` pending review)
- Red: status blocked (`agent:blocked`)

Document the taxonomy in the spec authoring guide (PTN-APP-GOV-005 companion) so spec authors know which routing label to apply alongside `agent-task`.
page_texts.21:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#step-2--implement-the-validation-stage]

### Step 2 — Implement the Validation Stage

The validation stage is a short-lived pipeline job. It must complete in under 30 seconds to give spec authors timely feedback. Reference the validation gate implementation in PTN-GOV-AI-007 Step 2 for the minimum implementation.

Extend the base validation with routing validation: if `agent-task` is present but no routing label is present, the pipeline should post a comment listing the available routing labels and halt rather than invoking a default agent.
page_texts.22:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#step-3--implement-the-dispatch-stage]

### Step 3 — Implement the Dispatch Stage

The dispatch stage is agent-type specific. Each routing label maps to a distinct agent configuration:

- **Context assembly**: Assemble the context window from the validated spec body, the enterprise context files (`.github/copilot-instructions.md` or equivalent), and any standards documents referenced in the Constraints section
- **Agent invocation**: Invoke the appropriate agent CLI, API, or workflow action with the assembled context
- **Output capture**: Capture the agent-produced file changes to a feature branch

For the first implementation, start with a single agent type (documentation or infrastructure) to validate the pipeline mechanics before expanding to implementation agents where the blast radius of incorrect output is higher.
page_texts.23:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#step-4--implement-the-report-stage]

### Step 4 — Implement the Report Stage

The report stage must always execute — even on agent failure. A pipeline that silently fails leaves the issue author with no signal.

**On success:**
1. Create the PR on the feature branch with the naming convention and traceability block
2. Post a success comment on the issue with the PR link and the Acceptance Criteria checklist for reviewers

**On failure:**
1. Apply the `agent:blocked` label to the issue
2. Post a failure comment identifying the failure stage and any available diagnostic information
3. Do not create a PR
page_texts.24:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#step-5--apply-branch-protection-equivalence]

### Step 5 — Apply Branch Protection Equivalence

Agent-produced PRs must go through the same branch protection gates as human-authored PRs (per ADR-GOV-008):
- Required status checks (automated tests, security scan, lint)
- Required reviewer approvals (minimum 1 human reviewer)
- No auto-merge without passing all checks

The agent pipeline must not be granted merge permissions. The agent creates the PR; a human approves and merges. This is the governance control that makes autonomous agent delivery safe for production delivery pipelines.
page_texts.25:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#step-6--post-dispatch-validation-optional]

### Step 6 — Post-Dispatch Validation (Optional)

After the agent produces output and the PR is created, a post-validation stage can verify that the agent's implementation addresses all scenarios defined in the originating spec. This step is optional but recommended for high-criticality work items.

**Post-validation checks:**
1. **Acceptance Criteria coverage** — parse the spec's Acceptance Criteria and verify each criterion has a corresponding test or implementation artifact in the PR
2. **Scenario completeness** — if the spec defines multiple scenarios (e.g., happy path, error handling, edge cases), confirm the PR contains evidence of each
3. **Contract conformance** — if the spec defines API contracts, schemas, or interface signatures, validate the implementation matches

**Implementation options:**
- **Automated**: A lightweight validation agent (or script) that runs against the PR diff and the original spec, producing a coverage report posted as a PR comment
- **Semi-automated**: CI checks that flag uncovered scenarios for human reviewer attention
- **Manual**: Reviewer checklist generated from spec Acceptance Criteria and attached to the PR

When automated post-validation detects gaps, the pipeline should post an advisory comment on the PR identifying uncovered scenarios — it should not block the PR or auto-close it. The human reviewer retains final authority on whether gaps are acceptable.

> **Note:** While acceptance-criteria coverage validation described above is optional, security and quality status checks (unit tests, integration tests, dependency vulnerability scan, code quality lint, and SAST for repositories handling sensitive data) remain **mandatory** for all agent-produced PRs per [GUID-SEC-AI-AGENTPIPE-2.9.08](../../../strategy/guidance/security/GUID-SEC-AI-AGENTPIPE-2.9.08-ai-agent-pipeline-security.md) §CTL-4.2. These mandatory checks are enforced via branch protection rules, not via this optional post-dispatch validation step.
page_texts.26:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#step-7--monitor-and-tune]

### Step 7 — Monitor and Tune

Track the following pipeline health metrics from the first sprint of operation:

| Metric | Definition | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Validation failure rate | % of `agent-task` issues that fail Stage 1 | Declining sprint-over-sprint |
| Agent success rate | % of dispatched agent invocations that produce a PR | > 80% in first sprint; > 95% at steady state |
| PR pass rate (first submission) | % of agent PRs that pass all branch protection gates without rework | Tracked; used to tune spec templates |
| Time-to-PR | Elapsed time from label assignment to PR creation | Baseline in first sprint; improve from there |

---
page_texts.28:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#minimum-privilege-agent-credentials]

### Minimum-Privilege Agent Credentials

Agent pipeline credentials must be scoped to the minimum permissions required:

| Permission | Granted | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `contents: write` (feature branches only) | Yes | Agent must commit to a feature branch |
| `pull-requests: write` | Yes | Agent must open a PR |
| `issues: write` | Yes | Pipeline must post comments and apply labels |
| `contents: write` (default/main branch) | **No** | Agents do not merge; humans do |
| `admin` | **No** | No administrative access required |

Use the principle of least privilege. If the CI/CD platform supports fine-grained token scoping, scope to the repository only, not the organization.
page_texts.29:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#prompt-injection-hardening]

### Prompt Injection Hardening

The issue body is passed to an AI model as context. It is untrusted user input. Before assembling the context window:

1. **Strip HTML**: Remove any HTML tags from the issue body
2. **Escape control sequences**: Remove or escape sequences that could be interpreted as model instructions (e.g., text that begins with "Ignore all previous instructions")
3. **Never execute issue body content**: Issue body content must not be passed to a shell interpreter, an eval function, or any execution context other than the model API
4. **Log the sanitized context**: Record the exact context window passed to the model in the provenance record (PTN-GOV-AI-005) — this enables incident investigation if an injection attempt is detected
page_texts.30:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#audit-trail]

### Audit Trail

Every pipeline execution must produce a log entry containing:
- The triggering issue URL and issue number
- The label that triggered the pipeline
- The validation result (pass/fail + details)
- The agent type invoked (if validation passed)
- The PR URL created (if dispatch succeeded)
- The timestamp of each stage completion

This log is the raw material for the compliance audit trail and for the provenance record (PTN-GOV-AI-005).

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#use-case-1--documentation-generation]

### Use Case 1 — Documentation Generation

An engineer creates Issue #102 using the PTN-APP-GOV-005 template with goal "Generate API reference documentation for the claims-processor service." Labels applied: `agent-task`, `agent:documentation`. The pipeline validates the spec (WI#4899 present, all sections complete), assembles a context window including the documentation standards reference from the Constraints section, invokes the documentation agent, and opens PR #108 with the generated docs. The issue receives a comment: "✅ Agent completed. PR #108 opened — 3 documentation files generated."
page_texts.33:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#use-case-2--routing-failure-no-routing-label]

### Use Case 2 — Routing Failure (No Routing Label)

An engineer applies `agent-task` to Issue #110 but forgets to add a routing label. The validation stage passes the spec check, but the routing check detects no routing label and posts the following comment before halting:

```
⚠️ Agent Dispatch Incomplete — No Routing Label

The `agent-task` label was applied but no agent routing label was found.
Please apply one of the following labels to route to the appropriate agent:

- `agent:implementation` — code changes
- `agent:documentation` — documentation generation
- `agent:testing` — test generation
- `agent:infrastructure` — infrastructure provisioning

Re-applying `agent-task` after adding a routing label will re-trigger the pipeline.
```
page_texts.34:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#use-case-3--agent-failure]

### Use Case 3 — Agent Failure

The implementation agent for Issue #115 fails with a model API timeout after 120 seconds. The pipeline applies the `agent:blocked` label and posts:

```
❌ Agent Execution Failed — Stage 2 (Dispatch)

Failure reason: Model API timeout after 120s
Agent type: implementation

The spec has been validated. Re-applying `agent-task` will retry dispatch.
If the failure persists, check model API status and review spec complexity.
```

The spec is preserved; no partial output is committed. The engineer removes and re-applies `agent-task` when the API recovers.

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-002-label-driven-agent-dispatch-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem**: Autonomous AI agents need an event-driven execution trigger that fires without human mediation when a work item is ready — but CI/CD pipelines are built around code events, not work item state changes.

**Solution**: A three-stage pipeline triggered by label assignment on an issue: **Validate** (spec structure + enterprise work item reference, fail closed), **Dispatch** (routing by secondary label → agent invocation with assembled context), **Report** (PR creation + issue comment). The label `agent-task` is the trigger; routing labels (`agent:implementation`, `agent:documentation`, etc.) select the agent configuration.

**Key Rule**: Agents never merge. The pipeline creates a PR; a human approves. This is the governance gate that makes autonomous delivery safe.

**Where it fits**: This pattern is the pipeline that wires everything together. PTN-APP-GOV-005 defines the spec it validates. PTN-GOV-AI-007 defines the cross-reference it enforces. PTN-APP-GOV-002 defines the enterprise context it injects.
